1: # Audit A: per-object natural-language verification
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `nl0-audit-a-8`.
7: 
8: This section is the single authority for what an accepted NL0 must satisfy.
9: Authoring instructions explain how to meet it; the audit checks these same
10: requirements. The table IDs also name executable coverage groups. Detailed
11: definitions in self-containment, logical rules and external-theorem review are
12: annexes to these requirements, not alternative permission policies.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the original target, every original H, quantifier, domain, range, normalization, endpoint and supplied core proof route. Parameters name ambient data; they cannot hide an H or a desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | original_context_note | Give each global object one complete typed definition and each local object a legitimate scoped introduction. Prove or directly assume every construction guard before use. Defining an object grants none of its properties. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Every selected M/E has an explicit faithful full statement and verified primary/native identity, context and hypotheses. Native typeclass premises are mathematical premises too. Record inaccessible checks as UNVERIFIED; they do not support an unqualified whole-proof pass. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | H/E/M are the only proposition roots. Every N/P has one producer, every retained non-H node lies in P's AND dependency closure, and every local proof uses its actual direct inputs. Keep every original H, including an unused H, and report which are unused. An ancestor is not automatically an input. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Every input and exported N/P states all formulas, quantifiers, conditions and semantic identifications needed by its consumers. A map or identity only present in the producer's body is unavailable to another node. Original text, equation labels and external notation cannot supply content. |
21: | `object_closure` | closure | declaration_check | Reverse-check actual object occurrences against global, statement-bound or local declarations. Types, domains, witness existence, first/last use and parameter dependencies agree. A name in a ledger is not an introduction or existence proof. |
22: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Ground factual uses in direct H/E/M/N, earlier in-scope local proofs, permitted elementary reasoning, or positively checked background notes under verified-background-1. Inspect actual prose and conditions; an inventory is not its proof. |
23: | `inputs` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Direct input statements are faithfully instantiated with compatible objects and assumptions. An internal input exports exactly its stated conclusion, not its producer's unexported facts. |
24: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Establish every output clause at ordinary rigorous natural-language granularity. Check material domains, limits, regularity, uniformity, integrability, signs, constants and degeneracies. Correct routine compression needs no exhaustive elementary calculation chain. |
25: | `dependency_accounting` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Every explicit input has a real role. Record eligible omitted basic library uses as verified background notes instead of rejecting solely for missing M accounting. No unverified source, extra H, core proof or project lemma can hide in prose, definitions or typeclasses. |
26: | `output` | inference | output_notes | The proved conclusion is the exact complete exported statement under its stated hypotheses, including all consumer-needed representations and identifications. Never weaken the target or strengthen an H to close the graph. |
27: | `scope` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Introduce and discharge temporary assumptions inside arguments. Close implications, cases, negations and quantifiers correctly; no witness or local assumption escapes. Original hypotheses remain explicit H inputs. |
28: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | For every actual M/E use, give the exact substitution and a direct input or displayed earlier derivation for every premise, plus any proved bridge to the claimed conclusion. Saying that a condition holds is not grounds for it. |
29: 
30: ### Scope of the same requirements
31: 
32: Global review checks the original target/H, source authenticity and complete
33: graph: H/E/M are its roots, and each N/P has its producer in that graph.
34: Its source judgments establish identity, full-statement fidelity and source
35: conditions; they do not re-prove each consumer's application. Its structure
36: judgment checks the actual AND graph and declared producer/input boundaries,
37: not whether a later packet reviewer has already returned PASS. Conditional
38: packet review owns each actual substitution, premise discharge, local proof
39: and output under those checked source statements. Final acceptance joins
40: all required source, structure and packet judgments; none replaces another.
41: Unfinished downstream assessment is not a reason to mark an already assessed
42: source identity or structural graph uncertain. Genuine source uncertainty
43: still blocks final acceptance. These assignments also govern author checks.
44: An original H remains explicitly present even when the proof does not use it;
45: report that unused condition. Do not invent a use or delete it to force graph
46: reachability. Selected E/M and internal N remain in the actual target closure.
47: Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary. Its task is the
48: implication from its explicitly supplied H/E/M/N statements to its output;
49: these statements are conditional premises. An input N is not a new global
50: root. Its producer body is intentionally absent and is neither required nor
51: available during this local check. Do not fail a valid conditional derivation
52: because its input theorem's producer or original source is outside the packet;
53: global review verifies source identity and producer membership, while the
54: producer's own packet review checks its proof. Conversely, do not import an absent N, an
55: ancestor's unexported fact or a theorem not present in the packet.
56: For example, a supplied N stating A and B permits deriving A by conjunction
57: elimination, without re-proving N. Having no such input does not permit
58: asserting A. The local requirements still check the complete actual argument,
59: all source-application premises, declarations, guards and discharged scopes.
60: These scopes are also the scopes of the author's corresponding self-checks.
61: 
62: The common elementary layer is the controller's `finite-language-3` profile:
63: equality, unfolding supplied definitions, routine finite semiring/ring/field
64: arithmetic, elementary ordered-field inequalities and explicit finite sums.
65: It grants no calculus, integral identity, measure, compactness, basis,
66: localization or tensor theorem. Use a verified input or a displayed local proof
67: for substantive facts. The verified-background admission rule below additionally
68: permits positively checked ordinary library facts without prior author M registration.
69: No theorem needs to be re-proved if its exact permitted source
70: and application already supply it. The schema describes representation; it
71: does not extend mathematical permissions.
72: 
73: The fixed profile is controller-owned. A packet/spec's `logic.calculations`,
74: `logic.primitives`, or prose claiming extra permissions is data to check
75: against that profile, never a second authority. Ordinary valid elementary
76: inferences may be compressed: do not demand a displayed chain for every midpoint
77: bound, rearrangement or elementary construction. Check that the conclusion
78: actually follows with the required signs and domains. A substantive missing
79: argument is not made elementary by naming its conclusion.
80: 
81: ### Verified background admission: verified-background-1
82: 
83: Keep all review dimensions. At A4 an omitted routine elementary explanation or
84: basic pinned-mathlib fact may PASS after positive mathematical checking. Record
85: useful routine completion or omitted library use in a node-local background note:
86: ID, exact argument location, precise fact, actual local condition grounds,
87: reviewer's justification, checked library evidence where applicable, optional

locals.declaration: Use m≥0 as the induction index for the formulas for h y^m v and x y^m v.

argument.text: H003 gives n>0 and I has n elements. We prove the two string formulas by induction. At m=0, h v=λv and xv=0 by H005. For the step temporarily assume L1: h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v, and, if m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v (with xy^0v=0 at m=0). From [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h in H004, h y^{m+1}v=y h y^m v-2y^{m+1}v=(λ-2m-2)y^{m+1}v, while x y^{m+1}v=y x y^m v+h y^m v=[m(λ-m+1)+λ-2m]y^m v=(m+1)(λ-m)y^m v. This also holds at m=0 using xv=0. Discharge L1; induction proves the asserted formulas for all nonnegative m.

produces.statement: n>0, card(I)=n; for every m≥0, h y^m v=(λ-2m)y^m v, and for every m≥1, x y^m v=m(λ-m+1)y^{m-1}v.

argument.text: For every i∈I, iteration of F001 gives x^i y^i v=i! λ(λ-1)⋯(λ-i+1)v. For i=0 this is v with empty product 1. For 1≤i≤λ each factor is a positive integer and hence nonzero in ℂ. H005 gives v≠0, so y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Their h-eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct in ℂ. To check independence, take any relation ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0 with complex coefficients and any j∈I; apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id). Every term except the j-th is zero; the remaining term is c_j∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. The product and e_j are nonzero, so c_j=0. Thus the whole family is linearly independent.

produces.statement: The family e:I→V is linearly independent over ℂ, each e_i is nonzero, and h e_i=(λ-2i)e_i for every i∈I.

argument.text: Apply M003 with A=ℂ, T=V, Q=I and f=e. F001 makes I finite and nonempty; F002 supplies independence; H004 and card(I)=n=λ+1 give the required dimension equality. Thus e spans V, so together with independence it is a basis. F001 at m=λ+1 says y^{λ+1}v, if nonzero, is an eigenvector of eigenvalue -λ-2. Expand this vector in the e-basis. Applying h-(-λ-2)Id shows each coefficient times (λ-2i+λ+2)=2(λ+1-i) is zero; these coefficients are nonzero scalars for i∈I. Hence every coordinate is zero and y^{λ+1}v=0. All higher powers vanish by further application of y.

produces.statement: The family e is a complex basis of V, and y^m v=0 for all integers m>λ.

argument.text: Divide the string identities F001 by i!: e_0=v, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, he_i=(λ-2i)e_i; directly ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, and ye_λ=0 by F003. For r≤i, iteration and division by r! give X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_{i-r}=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r}; if r>i the iteration passes xe_0=0. Similarly Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ, and otherwise is zero by F003. These binomial numbers are integers (they count r-element subsets of a set of the indicated nonnegative size). These are all the clauses of N001.

argument.text: Choose f as in F001. M001 with A=ℤ, B=R and T=M gives the R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Under ι_R these vectors go to f_i. If ∑ r_i f_i=0 with r_i∈R, complex independence of f gives every r_i=0. Hence ι_R is injective. Its image contains f and therefore spans V over ℂ. This also proves that M_R is free of rank n. From now on identify M_R with this image.

argument.text: Admissibility H006 makes every X_r,Y_r preserve M; their complex linearity then preserves the R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=[x,y]=xy-yx does too by H004. These integral operators obey the Chevalley brackets on M and therefore induce the stated action after tensoring. For any 0≤t≤λ, H003 gives t<p; applying M006 with ℓ=p to this arbitrary t and H001 gives p coprime to t!, hence p does not divide t!. Thus 1/t!∈R and t! is a unit. In particular λ!, j!, (λ-j)! are units for j∈I. The integer identity binom(λ,j)j!(λ-j)!=λ! shows that binom(λ,j) is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ-j)!/λ!.

argument.text: Compute on the complex e-basis of N001. X_λ kills all e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ sends e_0 to e_λ with coefficient 1. Thus Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}. Also X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient 1, so X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}. For E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}, an input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by the projection; if k>j it is sent beyond the end of the string and is zero. On e_j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Thus E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. Composing gives E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Every factor preserves M_R by F003, and its scalar lies in R. Hence all E_ij preserve M_R. This completes N002 without assuming any distinction of weights modulo p.

argument.text: Use the embedding of N002. E_ii maps M_R onto Jcoord_i e_i, because it extracts the i-th coordinate on the N001 basis. For i,j∈I and c∈Jcoord_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i belongs to M_R by N002, so c∈Jcoord_i. Interchanging i,j proves equality. N001 gives 0∈I and e_0=v, hence the common module is J. The projection E_00 of a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) gives finitely many generators of J e_0; since e_0≠0, their coefficients generate J. If J were zero every projection E_ii would vanish on M_R, and their sum is Id_V, so M_R would be zero. This contradicts its complex span V and n>0 from N001. Finally, coordinate projections show each element of M_R has coordinates in J; conversely each sum ∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J belongs to M_R. Uniqueness is complex independence of e. Thus M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

argument.text: Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map μ:T→ℂ is defined on simple tensors by μ(q⊗c)=qc. It is well-defined by additivity and R-balancing. Every tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors. Write its finitely many rational first factors over a common nonzero integer denominator d; balancing integer numerators into J writes the tensor as (1/d)⊗c for one c∈J. If its image in ℂ is zero, c/d=0, so c=0 and the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. If c_1,…,c_s is a finite R-generating family of J from F001, then 1⊗c_1,…,1⊗c_s spans T over ℚ by tensor bilinearity. In particular T is finitely generated as a ℚ-module, that is finite dimensional.

produces.statement: T=ℚ⊗_R J is a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space, and μ:T→ℂ, μ(q⊗c)=qc, is injective.

argument.text: The coordinate isomorphism in F001 induces an explicit ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R→∏_{i∈I}T: on q⊗∑c_i e_i it gives (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}. For clarity, define its inverse by summing the maps T→ℚ⊗_R M_R induced by c↦c e_i: a tuple (q_i⊗c_i)_i maps to ∑_i q_i⊗(c_i e_i), extended additively in each entry. Both maps are defined by balanced bilinear maps. On simple tensors their composites are identities, by uniqueness of the coordinates and finite distributivity; simple tensors generate, so these checks prove both inverse identities. This supplies the rationalized direct-sum identification, not just a count.

produces.statement: There is a ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R≃∏_{i∈I}T sending q⊗∑c_i e_i to (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}.

argument.text: Put r=dim_ℚ T. N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R indexed by I. Applying M001 with A=R and B=ℚ to this basis gives a ℚ-basis of ℚ⊗_R M_R indexed by I; M002 over ℚ therefore gives its dimension as card(I)=n, using N001. Apply M007 with A=ℚ to T to obtain freeness. The finite generation in F002 and this freeness verify the module premises of M004. Thus M004 with the constant family T over I gives dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}T)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. M005 applied to Φ from F003 equates these dimensions: n=nr. Because n>0, r=1.

produces.statement: dim_ℚ T=r=1.

argument.text: For any nonzero a∈J, injectivity of μ in F002 gives 1⊗a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent over ℚ: a scalar annihilating a nonzero vector in a vector space over a field is zero. Apply M003 with A=ℚ, ambient space T, the singleton index type and this singleton family. F004 gives the required dimension 1, so every 1⊗c with c∈J is q(1⊗a) for some q∈ℚ. Applying μ gives c=qa. Together with F001–F004 this proves every assertion of N003.

argument.text: Choose a≠0 in J and a family g as in F001. By the rational-line conclusion of N003, every g_j is q_j a for some q_j∈ℚ; because g_j and a are nonzero, q_j≠0. For a nonzero rational q=A/B with nonzero integers A,B, repeatedly remove factors p from A and B. This process terminates since p≥2 by H001 and absolute values strictly decrease at each removal. Thus A=p^s A', B=p^t B' with s,t≥0 and p dividing neither A' nor B'. Consequently q=p^{s-t}u with u=A'/B' a unit of R: both u and u^{-1}=B'/A' satisfy the denominator condition. Apply this to all the finitely many q_j, writing q_j=p^{ν_j}u_j with ν_j∈ℤ and u_j∈R×. The nonempty finite list of integer exponents has a minimum ν and an index j_0 attaining it.

Every generator g_j equals p^{ν_j-ν}u_j b with ν_j-ν≥0, so g_j∈Rb; conversely b∈J gives Rb⊂J. Therefore J=Rb. Substituting into the unique-coordinate decomposition of N003 proves that every element of M_R is a unique R-linear combination of b e_i: if ∑r_i b e_i=0, N003 gives r_i b=0 for each i, hence r_i=0 since b≠0. argument.text: For every integer d not divisible by p its image in K is nonzero, because H002 says the kernel of ℤ→K is pℤ. Thus define ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Equality of fractions is preserved by cross-multiplication, so this is well-defined and preserves sums and products; it extends ℤ→K. The characteristic also factors the integer map through ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ; primality H001 makes this a field, and its map into K is injective since a unital map from a field has zero kernel. On elementary tensors define A:M⊗_ℤK→M_R⊗_R K by A(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. The balancing relations in the two tensor products verify well-definedness; the inverse identities follow on the displayed generators, since (r⊗m)⊗c=(1⊗m)⊗ρ(r)c. These generators span, so A is a K-linear isomorphism.

argument.text: The kernel of ρ is pR: for a/d∈R, its image is zero exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/d belongs to pR. Its image is the prime field ℱ_p, because a/d reduces to the quotient of two prime-field elements. Thus R/pR≃ℱ_p. The map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K sends u⊗c to [u]⊗c. Conversely define [u]⊗c↦u⊗c. A different lift u+pw gives the same tensor since (pw)⊗c=w⊗pc=0. Balancing over ℱ_p is valid: lift a prime-field scalar to r∈R and use (ru)⊗c=u⊗ρ(r)c; changing its lift by pR has no effect. These formulas define inverse K-linear maps on the simple tensors. This proves the second isomorphism as well as its compatibility with the first one.

argument.text: Choose b as in N004 and define β_i=A^{-1}((b e_i)⊗1). M001 with A=R, B=K and basis (b e_i) gives the K-basis 1⊗b e_i of K⊗_R M_R; the tensor flip sends it to (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. The flip is an isomorphism because u⊗c↦c⊗u and its reverse are balanced and their composites fix all simple tensors. Transporting along A^{-1} therefore shows that β is a K-basis of V(K). M002 over K counts it: dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0 by N001. Also the quotient M_R/pM_R has the basis [b e_i] over R/pR: coordinates in the R-basis of N004 reduce independently, since a combination lies in pM_R exactly when every coefficient lies in pR. Thus β is precisely the reduced basis extended from ℱ_p to K as in the supplied proof.

Therefore the x,y,h formulas on β and the X_r,Y_r formulas are exactly those of N001 with each integer coefficient replaced by its image in K. For 0≤r≤λ, N002 makes r! a unit in R, so its image is nonzero in the field K. The integer-operator identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold on M and persist after tensoring. Thus X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r.

argument.text: Choose w,c,j from F001 within the nonzero branch. argument.text: Use the embedding of N002. E_ii maps M_R onto Jcoord_i e_i, because it extracts the i-th coordinate on the N001 basis. The projection E_00 of a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) gives finitely many generators of J e_0; since e_0≠0, their coefficients generate J. If J were zero every projection E_ii would vanish on M_R, and their sum is Id_V, so M_R would be zero. This contradicts its complex span V and n>0 from N001. Finally, coordinate projections show each element of M_R has coordinates in J; conversely each sum ∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J belongs to M_R. Uniqueness is complex independence of e. argument.text: Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map μ:T→ℂ is defined on simple tensors by μ(q⊗c)=qc. It is well-defined by additivity and R-balancing. Every tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors. These generators span, so A is a K-linear isomorphism.

argument.text: The kernel of ρ is pR: for a/d∈R, its image is zero exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/d belongs to pR. Its image is the prime field ℱ_p, because a/d reduces to the quotient of two prime-field elements. Thus R/pR≃ℱ_p. The map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K sends u⊗c to [u]⊗c. Conversely define [u]⊗c↦u⊗c. A different lift u+pw gives the same tensor since (pw)⊗c=w⊗pc=0. Balancing over ℱ_p is valid: lift a prime-field scalar to r∈R and use (ru)⊗c=u⊗ρ(r)c; changing its lift by pR has no effect. These formulas define inverse K-linear maps on the simple tensors. This proves the second isomorphism as well as its compatibility with the first one.

M002 over K counts it: dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0 by N001. Also the quotient M_R/pM_R has the basis [b e_i] over R/pR: coordinates in the R-basis of N004 reduce independently, since a combination lies in pM_R exactly when every coefficient lies in pR. argument.text: N002 expresses E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j} with the scalar a unit in R. H005 gives v≠0, so y^iv and e_i are nonzero. Their h-eigenvalues λ-2i are pairwise distinct in ℂ. To check independence, fix arbitrary c:I→ℂ and j∈I, and temporarily assume L2: ∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i=0. Apply ∏_{k∈I,k≠j}(h-(λ-2k)Id). Every term except the j-th is zero; the remaining term is c_j∏_{k≠j}2(k-j)e_j=0. The product and e_j are nonzero, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary every coefficient is zero. Discharging L2 and quantifying over c proves that the whole family is linearly independent.

produces.statement: The family e:I→V is linearly independent over ℂ, each e_i is nonzero, and h e_i=(λ-2i)e_i for every i∈I.

argument.text: Apply M003 with A=ℂ, T=V, Q=I and f=e. F001 makes I finite and nonempty; F002 supplies independence; H004 and card(I)=n=λ+1 give the required dimension equality. Thus e spans V, so together with independence it is a basis. F001 at m=λ+1 says y^{λ+1}v, if nonzero, is an eigenvector of eigenvalue -λ-2. Expand this vector in the e-basis. Applying h-(-λ-2)Id shows each coefficient times (λ-2i+λ+2)=2(λ+1-i) is zero; these eigenvalue-difference factors are nonzero scalars for i∈I. Hence every coordinate is zero and y^{λ+1}v=0. All higher powers vanish by further application of y.

produces.statement: The family e is a complex basis of V, and y^m v=0 for all integers m>λ.

argument.text: Divide the string identities F001 by i!: e_0=v, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ, he_i=(λ-2i)e_i; directly ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, and ye_λ=0 by F003. For r≤i, iteration and division by r! give X_r e_i=[(λ-i+1)⋯(λ-i+r)/r!]e_{i-r}=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r}; if r>i the iteration passes xe_0=0. Similarly Y_r e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_{i+r}=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} when i+r≤λ, and otherwise is zero by F003. These binomial numbers are integers (they count r-element subsets of a set of the indicated nonnegative size). This proves the basis, termination and all the asserted action formulas.

argument.text: Choose f as in F001. M001 with A=ℤ, B=R and T=M gives the R-basis (1⊗f_i)_{i∈I} of M_R. Under ι_R these vectors go to f_i. argument.text: Admissibility H006 makes every X_r,Y_r preserve M; their complex linearity then preserves the R-span M_R. In particular x=X_1 and y=Y_1 preserve M, and h=[x,y]=xy-yx does too by H004. These integral operators obey the Chevalley brackets on M and therefore induce the stated action after tensoring. For any 0≤t≤λ, H003 gives t<p; applying M006 with ℓ=p to this arbitrary t and H001 gives p coprime to t!, hence p does not divide t!. Thus 1/t!∈R and t! is a unit. argument.text: Compute on the complex e-basis of N001. X_λ kills all e_k with k<λ and sends e_λ to e_0 with coefficient binom(λ,λ)=1; Y_λ sends e_0 to e_λ with coefficient 1. Thus Y_λ X_λ=E_{λλ}. Also X_{λ-i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient 1, so X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}. For E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}, an input e_k with k<j is sent below e_λ and killed by the projection; if k>j it is sent beyond the end of the string and is zero. On e_j the coefficient is binom(λ,λ-j)=binom(λ,j). Thus E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}. Composing gives E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Every factor preserves M_R by F003, and its scalar lies in R. Hence all E_ij preserve M_R. These identities and preservation statements require no distinction of weights modulo p.

argument.text: Use the embedding of N002. E_ii maps M_R onto Jcoord_i e_i, because it extracts the i-th coordinate on the N001 basis. For i,j∈I and c∈Jcoord_j, E_ij(c e_j)=c e_i belongs to M_R by N002, so c∈Jcoord_i. Interchanging i,j proves equality. N001 gives 0∈I and e_0=v, hence the common module is J. The projection E_00 of a finite R-basis of M_R (N002) gives finitely many generators of J e_0; since e_0≠0, their coefficients generate J. Temporarily assume L1: J={0}. Then every projection E_ii would vanish on M_R, and their sum is Id_V, so M_R would be zero. This contradicts its complex span V and n>0 from N001. Discharge L1 to conclude J≠{0}. Finally, coordinate projections show each element of M_R has coordinates in J; conversely each sum ∑ c_i e_i with c_i∈J belongs to M_R. Uniqueness is complex independence of e. Thus M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

argument.text: Put T=ℚ⊗_R J. The multiplication map μ:T→ℂ is defined on simple tensors by μ(q⊗c)=qc. It is well-defined by additivity and R-balancing. Every tensor is a finite sum of simple tensors. Write its finitely many rational first factors over a common nonzero integer denominator d; balancing integer numerators into J writes the tensor as (1/d)⊗c for one c∈J. If its image in ℂ is zero, c/d=0, so c=0 and the tensor is zero. Thus μ is injective. If c_1,…,c_s is a finite R-generating family of J from F001, then 1⊗c_1,…,1⊗c_s spans T over ℚ by tensor bilinearity. In particular T is finitely generated as a ℚ-module, that is finite dimensional.

argument.text: The coordinate isomorphism in F001 induces an explicit ℚ-linear equivalence Φ:ℚ⊗_R M_R→∏_{i∈I}T: on q⊗∑c_i e_i it gives (q⊗c_i)_{i∈I}. For clarity, define its inverse by summing the maps T→ℚ⊗_R M_R induced by c↦c e_i: a tuple (q_i⊗c_i)_i maps to ∑_i q_i⊗(c_i e_i), extended additively in each entry. Both maps are defined by balanced bilinear maps. On simple tensors their composites are identities, by uniqueness of the coordinates and finite distributivity; simple tensors generate, so these checks prove both inverse identities. This supplies the rationalized direct-sum identification, not just a count.

argument.text: Put r=dim_ℚ T. N002 supplies an R-basis of M_R indexed by I. Applying M001 with A=R and B=ℚ to this basis gives a ℚ-basis of ℚ⊗_R M_R indexed by I; M002 over ℚ therefore gives its dimension as card(I)=n, using N001. Apply M007 with A=ℚ to T to obtain freeness. The finite generation in F002 and this freeness verify the module premises of M004. Thus M004 with the constant family T over I gives dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}T)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. M005 applied to Φ from F003 equates these dimensions: n=nr. Because n>0, r=1.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary a,z∈J and temporarily assume L2: a≠0. Injectivity of μ in F002 gives 1⊗a≠0, since its image is a. argument.text: For every integer d not divisible by p its image in K is nonzero, because H002 says the kernel of ℤ→K is pℤ. Thus define ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). Equality of fractions is preserved by cross-multiplication, so this is well-defined and preserves sums and products; it extends ℤ→K. The characteristic also factors the integer map through ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ; primality H001 makes this a field, and its map into K is injective since a unital map from a field has zero kernel. On elementary tensors define A:M⊗_ℤK→M_R⊗_R K by A(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. The balancing relations in the two tensor products verify well-definedness; the inverse identities follow on the displayed generators, since (r⊗m)⊗c=(1⊗m)⊗ρ(r)c. These generators span, so A is a K-linear isomorphism.

argument.text: The kernel of ρ is pR: for a/d∈R, its image is zero exactly when p divides a, equivalently a/d belongs to pR. Its image is the prime field ℱ_p, because a/d reduces to the quotient of two prime-field elements. Thus R/pR≃ℱ_p. The map M_R⊗_R K→(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K sends u⊗c to [u]⊗c. Conversely define [u]⊗c↦u⊗c. A different lift u+pw gives the same tensor since (pw)⊗c=w⊗pc=0. Balancing over ℱ_p is valid: lift a prime-field scalar to r∈R and use (ru)⊗c=u⊗ρ(r)c; changing its lift by pR has no effect. These formulas define inverse K-linear maps on the simple tensors. This proves the second isomorphism as well as its compatibility with the first one.

The flip is an isomorphism because u⊗c↦c⊗u and its reverse are balanced and their composites fix all simple tensors. Transporting along A^{-1} therefore shows that β is a K-basis of V(K). M002 over K counts it: dim_K V(K)=card(I)=n>0 by N001. Also the quotient M_R/pM_R has the basis [b e_i] over R/pR: coordinates in the R-basis of N004 reduce independently, since a combination lies in pM_R exactly when every coefficient lies in pR. Thus β is precisely the reduced basis extended from ℱ_p to K as in the supplied proof.

argument.text: N001 gives all action formulas on e_i; complex linearity gives the identical formulas on b e_i. In particular the induced x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y and [x,y]=h on V(K), because tensor extension preserves sums and compositions of lattice endomorphisms. The maps A and B above commute with every induced lattice operator: check this on m⊗c and u⊗c using their defining formulas. Therefore the x,y,h formulas on β and the X_r,Y_r formulas are exactly those of N001 with each integer coefficient replaced by its image in K. Explicitly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} until yβ_λ=0, and hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i; X_r and Y_r have respectively coefficients bar(binom(λ-i+r,r)) and bar(binom(i+r,r)) in their stated ranges and zero outside. For 0≤r≤λ, N002 makes r! a unit in R, so its image is nonzero in the field K. The integer-operator identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r hold on M and persist after tensoring. Thus X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r.

argument.text: N002 expresses E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j} with the scalar a unit in R. It is then invariant under their nonnegative powers, their scalar multiples, and their compositions. Every divided power appearing in this formula has index between 0 and λ, so F004 shows that it preserves W. Consequently every T_ij preserves W. Discharge L1 and quantify over W. This proves the tensor identifications, reduced basis and formulas, and the matrix-unit invariance assertion.

original_context.full_target: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer λ with 0≤λ<p, the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module V=V(λ) of dimension λ+1 with Chevalley generators x,y,h, every nonzero v∈V with xv=0 and hv=λv, and every arbitrary admissible lattice M⊂V (a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all x^r/r!,y^r/r!), prove that V(K)=M⊗ℤK is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is zero or V(K). Here L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗ℤK acts by the induced lattice operators, including the Chevalley construction in characteristic 2. No algebraic closure assumption on K is made, and λ=0 and p=2 are included.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime.
The characteristic of the field K is p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The elements x,y,h are its Chevalley generators and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h.
v≠0, xv=0, and hv=λv.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. It is arbitrary and is not required to be the minimal lattice.

original_context.conclusion: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, including λ=0 and p=2, over the given arbitrary field K.
